A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same VisRet work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original retrieval and VQA experiments in Table 1, Figure 2, and Appendix B, including model comparisons and qualitative examples.

after.justification: V2 retains original retrieval and VQA results and reports additional COCO-Hard, baseline, and image-generator experiments in Tables 2 and 5.

M1.justification: Both versions use LLM-generated visualization instructions, image generation, image-to-image retrieval, and reciprocal rank fusion. V2's explicit sampling of multiple images from one instruction was already documented in v1 Appendix C; expanded explanations and generator comparisons do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: V2 adds COCO-Hard caption-to-image retrieval involving everyday scenes and spatial relationships among objects, substantially broadening v1's natural-species coverage. Visual-RAG, Visual-RAG-ME, and INQUIRE-Rerank-Hard remain; the multi-entity benchmark description is relocated, not newly introduced.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds BLIP corpus captioning, VISA top-30 reranking, and captioning-based top-30 reranking to the retained comparisons. Query Expansion/LLM Rephrase is renamed LLM Rewriting. The corresponding generator-choice table also drops v1's LLM Rephrase reference row.

E3.justification: New protocols include selecting 500 difficult COCO queries from 5,000 using nDCG@30 and evaluating top-30 reranking. The generator study changes from Visual-RAG with CLIP to Visual-RAG-ME with CLIP and E5-V, expands model configurations, and adds an average across three nDCG cutoffs. Default VisRet and VQA settings remain stable.

E4.justification: The generator sensitivity study is substantially replaced and expanded, adding FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Gemini, and E5-V evaluations. V2 also evaluates a caption-only VISA ablation and adds COCO qualitative cases. The query-LLM, VQA-reader, and generated-images-as-knowledge analyses largely retain v1's evidence despite moving into Section 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Multiple generated query images are part of the retained retrieval procedure, not newly reported experimental replications.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline and COCO results and replaces the generator-study results under different conditions. For example, COCO-Hard CLIP nDCG@30 is 0.108 for VisRet, 0.042 for Original Query, and 0.153 for BLIP. Retained main-comparison nDCG scores are unchanged, and VQA tables change only scale and rounding. Some earlier Recall@10/30 entries are no longer reported.

T1.justification: V2 adds an explicit nDCG@1 = Recall@1 convention with an 'undefined' rationale and writes synthesized queries as members of corpus I. These are limited additions to the formal description. The retrieval/RAG formulation and RRF equation otherwise remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central visualization-based retrieval and downstream VQA contributions remain. V2 extends its claimed superiority to captioning/reranking alternatives and four benchmarks. Headline gains change from relative NDCG@10 improvements over original-query retrieval to average absolute nDCG@30 improvements across the expanded baseline set.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving caption information loss, COCO training-domain similarity, and reranking candidate/cost limits. Its replacement generator study describes benefits from all tested generators, whereas v1 discussed weak-generator limitations on Visual-RAG. The ethics section removes explicit faithfulness/factuality concerns, while the limitation that generated images cannot fully replace retrieved knowledge remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds the COCO preparation recipe and baseline implementation information, including the BLIP checkpoint, minimum caption length, VISA implementation reference, Qwen model, and captioning prompt. Existing VisRet prompts, hardware, RRF setting, and release information remain. Some new model labels are inconsistent between passages, including Qwen 70B versus 72B and Stable Diffusion 3 versus 3.5.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for COCO, VISA, Qwen2.5-VL, FLUX, Qwen-Image, and Gemini, and removes several bias/factuality references. Positioning expands to caption-based retrieval alternatives, but the related-work taxonomy and distinction from embedding training, query expansion, reranking, and generative indexing remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, changes author order, rewrites the abstract, and substantially reorganizes the narrative. Visual-RAG-ME construction moves from Appendix A into Section 4, most appendix analyses become Section 6, and experimental setup and results gain more explicit organization. Implementation and qualitative appendices are reorganized accordingly.

P2.justification: The main results table is redesigned with colored method families, additional rows and COCO columns, and removal of separate Recall columns. Dataset and analysis tables move into the main text; the generator table gains retriever blocks and an average column. Example tables expand, and Figure 2 changes colors and legend layout while retaining its results.

improvement.justification: Broader coverage, additional comparison families, and clearer organization offer benefits, but important new evidence has unresolved inconsistencies. Table 5 reports Gemini/E5-V Avg as 0.589 although its listed scores average 0.622. Table 2's zero nDCG@30 results for stated top-30 reranking are unexplained despite nonzero initial-retrieval scores. V1's weak-generator study on Visual-RAG is also replaced. These tradeoffs prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
